Bambus.et: From early modern Dutch bamboes (contemporary bamboe), from Portuguese bambus, plural of bambu, from Malay bambu, from Kannada ಬಂಬು (bambu).

s: Bamberg (an independent town in the Upper Franconia region, Bavaria, Germany)
a rural district of the Upper Franconia region, Bavaria, surrounding but not including the town of Bamberg, which nevertheless serves as its administrative seat
fear, anxiety (especially relating to the outcome of some action)
to be afraid that something might happen
Bammel.et: Deverbal of regional bammeln (“to dangle”) (compare standard baumeln), referencing the uncertainty that comes with fear.

s: a native or inhabitant of Bamberg
a surname transferred from the place name.

Bamia.et: Borrowed from Arabic بَامِيَة (bāmiya) and its descendants. In the 19th century contact with the adjacent Ottoman Empire was a more likely source of acquaintance with the plant than international trade being fast enough to introduce the term Okra for the peris…

Bambule.et: Borrowed from French bamboula, originally prison slang.
